forbidden.name: no-circular
forbidden.comment: Production and test modules must not form circular dependency chains.

forbidden.name: no-production-to-test
forbidden.comment: Production code must not import tests or test-only utilities.

forbidden.name: no-unresolved
forbidden.comment: Every dependency in analyzed source must resolve from the pinned toolchain.

forbidden.name: no-orphans
forbidden.comment: A module nothing imports and nothing runs is dead weight that still has to be reviewed, type-checked and kept compiling. Knip finds unused files it can trace from an entry point; this catches the ones that are reachable from nowhere at all. Type declarations and config files are legitimately orphaned.

forbidden.name: no-production-to-dev-dependency
forbidden.comment: src/ is the code this project ships. A devDependency is present on a developer's machine and in CI, and absent everywhere else, so importing one from src/ produces a module that works in every test and fails on first run. scripts/ is exempt: it only ever runs where devDependencies are installed.

forbidden.name: no-deprecated-core
forbidden.comment: Node core modules that have been deprecated. They keep working until the release that removes them, at which point the failure is a runtime crash rather than a build error.

forbidden.name: no-deprecated-npm
forbidden.comment: Depending on a package its own author has marked deprecated means depending on code that will not be fixed.

forbidden.name: no-duplicate-dependency-types
forbidden.comment: A package listed as both a dependency and a devDependency resolves differently depending on which manifest wins, which is a difference between CI and production that no test can see.

forbidden.name: not-to-spec
forbidden.comment: Test files must not be imported by anything. A shared helper belongs in a plainly named module, not in a file the test runner also collects.

forbidden.name: no-lib-to-entry-point
forbidden.comment: scripts/lib/ holds the tested decision logic and scripts/*.ts are the argv-and-exit shells around it. The dependency runs one way: a library module that imports an entry point would execute that entry point's top-level main() as a side effect of being imported by a test.
